query_text: What medicine should I take when I get a cold?

message.content:
Based on information from health authorities, here are the main options for treating cold symptoms:

## Over-the-Counter Medicines

**For pain, fever, and aches:**
- **Acetaminophen (Tylenol/paracetamol)** or **ibuprofen (Advil/Motrin)** can help relieve headaches, sore throat, and reduce fever

**For nasal congestion:**
- **Decongestants** (like pseudoephedrine or phenylephrine) in tablet form or as nasal sprays/drops can help unblock your nose
- Important: Don't use nasal decongestant sprays for more than 3-5 days to avoid "rebound congestion"

**For runny nose/sneezing:**
- **Antihistamines** may help, though they aren't very effective for cold symptoms specifically

**For cough:**
- **Cough suppressants** (to reduce coughing) or **expectorants** (to loosen mucus)
- **Honey** can relieve cough for adults and children over 1 year old

## Important Safety Notes

- **Antibiotics do NOT work for colds** — colds are caused by viruses, not bacteria
- There's no cure for the common cold; medicines only relieve symptoms while your body fights the infection
- Most colds improve on their own within 7-10 days
- Check with a pharmacist or doctor if you have other health conditions (especially high blood pressure, as decongestants can raise it) or take other medications
- Avoid giving aspirin to children or teenagers

## Non-Drug Relief

- Rest and plenty of fluids
- Saline nasal sprays or rinses
- Humidifier or steam from a hot shower
- Warm salt water gargling for sore throat
- Hot lemon and honey drinks

**When to see a doctor:** If symptoms last more than 10 days, fever lasts more than 3-4 days, you have trouble breathing, or symptoms worsen after improving.

---

Sources:
1. https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/common-cold/
2. https://www.cdc.gov/common-cold/treatment/index.html
3. https://www.mayoclinic.org/diseases-conditions/common-cold/diagnosis-treatment/drc-20351611
4. https://www.webmd.com/cold-and-flu/decongestants-antihistamines-cold
5. https://www.webmd.com/cold-and-flu/cold-medicine-treatment-when-what-how
